title: Days Until Warmer
statement:
You get a forecast temps, one temperature per day. For each day, return how many days you have to wait for a strictly warmer day. If no later day is warmer, use 0 for that day.

Return an array wait of the same length, where wait[i] is the answer for day i.

examples.why: Day 2 (13) does not stop at day 3, because an equal temperature is not warmer; it waits until 17 on day 4. Nothing after 17 is warmer, and 11 is the last day.
Three days are left waiting, and one warm day answers all of them at once. That is the moment a stack shines.
No day is ever strictly warmer than another.

hints: The simple way scans forward from every day. Which days does that scan look at again and again?
Look at the days that are still waiting at some moment. If a colder day sits after a warmer one, which will be answered first? What shape does the waiting list have?

Keep the indices of waiting days on a stack; their temperatures never increase from bottom to top. When today is warmer than the top, today answers it: pop and record the distance. Repeat, then push today.

explain.intuition:
Walk through the days and keep a list of days that have not found a warmer day yet. That list is always non-increasing in temperature from oldest to newest: if a newer day were warmer than an older waiting day, it would have answered it already.

So when today arrives, only the newest waiting days can be answered, and they come off one by one from the end until the newest remaining one is at least as warm as today. That is a stack. Each day is pushed once and popped at most once, so all the pops together cost O(n), even though a single day can pop many.
steps: Fill wait with zeros and create an empty stack of indices.
For each day i: while the stack is not empty and temps[i] > temps[top], pop top and set wait[top] = i − top.
Push i: it now waits for its own warmer day.
Days still on the stack at the end never got warmer; their 0 stays.
pitfalls: Popping on >= instead of >: an equal temperature would count as warmer.
Pushing temperatures instead of indices. You need the index to compute the distance.
Thinking the nested while loop makes it O(n²). Count pushes and pops instead: each index is pushed once and popped at most once.

solutions.title: Scan forward from every day
solutions.idea: For each day, walk right until a warmer day appears.

solutions.title: Monotonic stack of waiting days
solutions.idea: Keep the indices of days still waiting. Their temperatures never increase toward the top, so a warm day answers them from the top down.

solutions.title: Walk backwards and jump
solutions.idea: Fill answers from the right. To find the next warmer day after i, start at i + 1 and jump by the answers already computed: if day j is not warmer, nothing before j + wait[j] can be either.

followups: Return, for each day, how many days ago it was last warmer instead. What changes in the loop?
The forecast arrives as a stream and you must answer each day as soon as possible. Which days can you answer, and when?
